segments.text:
Verſ. 2.
For it ſhall bee as a bird that flieth, and a nest forſaken: the daughter of Moab ſhall be at the fords of Arnon.

THe Prophet now ſhewes what he meant to ſay, by his former deriſion; to wit, that the Moabites muſt not thinke of ſending ſacrifices then, becauſe they cannot otherwiſe ſaue themſelues, but by fleeing from their Country. By the ſimilitude of birds, he expreſſeth the terror wherewith they being once ſtrucken, ſhall flee at the noiſe of a leaſe. For hee threatens the fearefull and weariſome flight of the Moabites, who had abuſed their reſt.
